subject.title: sessions.patch has no plugin-ownership check, unlike its sessions.delete sibling

question: Should this public cross-plugin `sessions.patch` ownership bypass be handled as a narrow public gateway bugfix, or routed through security-owned advisory/backport handling first?
rationale: The source evidence supports a small code fix, but the affected behavior is a plugin isolation boundary on a stable gateway RPC surface, so automation should not choose the disclosure and release-handling path on its own.

options.title: Approve Narrow Public Fix
options.body: Patch `sessions.patch` to reuse the delete ownership invariant and add focused regression tests, while maintainers decide release-note or backport wording.

options.title: Route Through Security Handling
options.body: Pause public repair automation and handle advisory, disclosure, and backport decisions through the repository security process.

options.title: Declare Current Asymmetry Intentional
options.body: Keep the current behavior only if maintainers intentionally want plugin-runtime callers with admin scope to patch foreign sessions and can document why delete remains different.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Public Fix
recommendation.body: Patch `sessions.patch` to reuse the delete ownership invariant and add focused regression tests, while maintainers decide release-note or backport wording.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current routing signal from the adjacent archive-gated delete ownership work and recent session lifecycle changes.
